script.text: Iran says it hit U.S. bases in Bahrain. Is a tanker showdown next?

Iran's Revolutionary Guards say missiles and drones targeted two U.S. Patriot radars at bases in Bahrain on Saturday night. Bahrain says it intercepted several attacks. A civilian industrial site caught fire, and nobody was hurt. The radar claims are not verified.

At sea, the pressure kept rising. Britain's maritime agency UKMTO says two tankers were hit by unknown projectiles near Khasab, Oman, on Saturday. That is the second day in a row. Iran's army says a ship hit a mine.

Next could be Kharg Island. Euronews and Iran International, citing satellite images, report more than fourteen tankers lined up for a convoy. Iran's deputy foreign minister calls the U.S. blockade an act of war.
Will Iran's tanker convoy sail before December? Yes or no?

upload.title: Iran Fires at US Bases in Bahrain. Tanker Showdown Next? #shorts
upload.description:
Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) said on Saturday night, November 21, 2026, that it targeted two radars of U.S. Army Patriot air defence systems at the Al-Riffa and Awali/Sakhir bases in Bahrain with missiles and drones, citing earlier violations of Iranian airspace by U.S. MQ-1 and MQ-9 drones. Iranian media initially named other bases, and the IRGC's damage claims could not be independently verified. Bahrain's Defence Force said air defences intercepted several Iranian aerial attacks and falling debris caused minor material damage with no injuries; Bahrain's Interior Ministry said a civilian industrial facility caught fire. The same day, the UK Maritime Trade Operations centre (UKMTO) reported two tankers struck by unknown projectiles near Khasab, Oman, while leaving the Strait of Hormuz, the second straight day of such incidents; no casualties were reported. Iran's army said a ship caught fire after hitting a mine. Euronews and Iran International, citing satellite imagery and ship tracking, reported that more than 14 Iranian oil tankers have gathered at Kharg Island for a convoy to test the U.S. naval blockade of Iranian ports; no Iranian official has confirmed the convoy. Iran's deputy foreign minister Kazem Gharibabadi called the blockade an "act of war". Locations on the map are approximate.
